attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated firmly with 'I fully believe'.

semantics.note: In context, 'this' means the AI bubble. The normalised sole-cause claim matches the statement, with no hedge left out.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats this as a single-cause counterfactual that can't be observed while OpenAI survives, and gives no measure of the bubble 'keeping going'. Grading it not adjudicable is reasonable.

reviews.rationale: The claim says OpenAI's survival is the only reason the AI bubble continues. That can only be tested by seeing what happens if OpenAI collapses, which has not happened, and the bubble has no stated measure. The packet has no outcome evidence, and the one non-OpenAI spending source it considered does not test the counterfactual. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter.

semantics.note: From context, the four companies are NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom and Disney. 'Between misleading and fictional' is fairly reduced to 'misleading or fictional'. The 'all three' slip later in the sentence is noted.

contract.note: Reading 'misleading' as non-binding, dropped, sharply cut, or not proceeding as announced by the post date is ordinary and fair. It applies the speaker's own 'all four' and splits the claim into a rally part and a deal part.

evidence.note: NVIDIA shares rose about 4% on the September 2025 announcement.
NVIDIA's CFO said the deal was still only a letter of intent two months later, which fits 'misleading'.
FT, relayed: the $100B framework was shelved for a $30B stake, so it did not go ahead as announced. Secondhand source.
Disney shares rose on the announcement. No size is given, so this is weak but fits.
The Disney deal ended in March 2026, which counts as dropped under the contract. It was signed at the time, so 'fictional' overstates it.
AMD shares jumped 24% on the deal.
Broadcom shares rose more than 10% on the deal.
AMD's filing calls it a definitive agreement, with first deployment due in the second half of 2026. Nothing in the packet shows it collapsed by the post date. This is a company disclosure.
In June 2026 a physical chip was delivered and the companies still aimed for deployment by end-2026, roughly on schedule, so the Broadcom deal was proceeding.
Dated after the post: OpenAI still planned AMD deployment. Outside the target period, so context only.

reviews.rationale: Part 1 holds: all four stocks rose on their deal announcements (e1, e4, e6, e7). Part 2 holds only for NVIDIA, where the letter of intent was shelved (e2, e3), and Disney, where the deal was dropped (e5). AMD's was a definitive agreement still on schedule (e8), and Broadcom's was going ahead with a chip delivered (e9). So 'all four' deals being misleading fails for two of the four.
